tspan.tspan: Predicting Interstitial ELF and Mapping Void

text.tspan: Electron localization function (ELF) prediction with an atom–void graph network, and exact geometric void connectivity
In an electride, extra electrons sit in the empty space between
atoms and act as anions. Whether those regions are isolated
(0D) or connected (1D, 2D) shapes the material’s properties.
GOAL screen crystals for electrides from structure alone, without DFT on every candidate. We built two void-centered tools and tested each one separately.

tspan.tspan: Can a graph network predict ELF at each candidate void

g.inkscape:label: Closing bottleneck concept
g.text: open channel (same geometry in both rows)
Geometry shows where a path could exist
ELF shows whether electrons occupy it
Predict ELF at bottlenecks, not just voids
Validate against DFT on known electrides
Combine both into one electride screen
Find the channel and its bottleneck
